clue.text: Having much to hide?

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin, so someone with a great deal of hide has a heavy covering, the figurative sense being someone not easily hurt

explanation.surface: A question about a person with a lot of secrets to conceal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' reads as a verb about secrets, but here it is the noun meaning skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Insensitive people are figuratively said to have tough, thick outer layers that criticism cannot pierce.

clue.text: To turn over room would reveal protective bits of footwear

indicators.note: to turn something over flips it, so the word for room is written backwards

parts.note: room means space

explanation.surface: Clearing out a storeroom exposes the reinforced ends of some boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn over' reverses SPACE to ECAPS, placed after TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel or leather caps cover the front of a boot to shield the wearer's foot.

clue.text: No time to abuse a king for not taking the broad view

indicators.note: 'No time' tells us to drop the letter for time from the word that follows

parts.note: to abuse someone is to insult them
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A narrow-minded person is accused of not finding a moment to insult the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No time' removes T from INSULT, leaving INSUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone parochial, like an island cut off from the mainland, has a narrow outlook.

clue.text: Abandoned lady? It might seem not

definitions.text: Abandoned lady? It might seem not

parts.words: Abandoned lady? It might seem not
parts.note: abandoned means both deserted and immoral; a mistress maintained by a lover is morally loose yet, as the label says, retained rather than deserted

explanation.surface: A question about whether a deserted woman is truly deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' suggests left behind; the answer is a loose woman who, by her name, has been held on to.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistress financially supported by her lover is the classic dissolute woman of older novels.

clue.text: Bake sizzling British dish

indicators.note: sizzling food is jumping about in a hot pan, so the letters of the word before are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to cook a hot British meal in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sizzling' rearranges BAKE into KEBA, then B is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Skewered or sliced grilled meat is a popular takeaway meal.

clue.text: Making sin seem to be retribution

indicators.note: making something out of the given letters means building a new word from them

explanation.surface: A moralising remark that making sin look attractive brings punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' tells us to form a word from the seven letters of SIN and SEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of vengeance, and her name now means deserved punishment.

clue.text: Charm of hair brushed up for us

indicators.note: in a down clue, hair brushed upward reads from bottom to top, reversing the word

parts.note: a mane is a head of hair
something for us is ours, our own

explanation.surface: A hairstyle swept upward is meant to win us over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brushed up' reverses MANE to ENAM, followed by OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate someone is to make them fall in love, so it is a verb of charming.

clue.text: Address oneself to a job and work in busy shire

parts.note: a post is a job

indicators.note: 'in' places the word for work inside the rearranged county
busy suggests bustling movement, so the letters of the county are jumbled

parts.note: OP is short for opus, Latin for a work

explanation.surface: Someone talks to themself about taking a post and working in a lively county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' rearranges SHIRE to RHISE, and 'in' puts OP inside it to make ROPHISE.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhetoric, to apostrophise is to turn and speak directly to someone absent or to an abstraction.

clue.text: Newsmen out of bed for some physical activity

parts.note: the press is the body of journalists
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: Journalists getting up for a bit of exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: This floor exercise raises the body using the arms, a standard part of a workout.

clue.text: Attack doctor in committee

indicators.note: 'in' puts the doctor inside the committee

parts.note: a board is a committee
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A physician on a board comes under assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To shell or pound a target heavily is to assail it.

clue.text: Church's removal of proposal?

parts.note: split as de- plus nomination, it would mean taking away a nomination; the whole word is a branch of the church

explanation.surface: A question about a church withdrawing a motion.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as DE (removal) plus NOMINATION (proposal), while its real sense is a religious body.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christian sect such as Methodism or Anglicanism is a separate church grouping.

clue.text: Pig runs round lobby showing no subtlety

indicators.note: the pig runs round the lobby, so its letters enclose the word for lobby

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
a hall is an entrance lobby

explanation.surface: A pig charging about a hallway is hardly discreet.
explanation.definitionFit: A superficial argument lacks depth, so it is lacking in nuance.

clue.text: Graduate's presently to be a tenor oboe

parts.note: a BA is a graduate, with the possessive S
presently means soon

explanation.surface: A graduate is shortly to become a tenor in an oboe band.
explanation.definitionFit: The bassoon is the lower-pitched member of the double-reed woodwind family to which the oboe belongs.

clue.text: Rhode Island sermon which could give you a bit of a lift

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for the US state
SER is a dictionary abbreviation for sermon

explanation.surface: A preacher in Rhode Island delivering an uplifting address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' sounds like elevation of the spirit; here it is the vertical part of one stair step.
explanation.definitionFit: In a staircase, the upright board between treads helps raise you a step.

clue.text: What could be drowned by me? Mortals maybe

definitions.text: What could be drowned by me? Mortals maybe

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters might form something else, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A whirlpool speaking, boasting that it might swallow humans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges ME and MORTALS; the whole clue is also what a whirlpool might say.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent whirlpool at sea can pull vessels and swimmers under the water.

clue.text: In East college women present significance of alibi

parts.note: the LSE is the London School of Economics, a college
present means here

explanation.surface: Someone claims they were at a London college with women at the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Alibi is Latin for 'in another place', which is what an alibi asserts.

clue.text: Yielders of cannabis harvest?

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis, so plants yielding pot would be cannabis plants; the real sense is houseplants grown in containers

explanation.surface: A question about what produces a crop of marijuana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' is slang for cannabis, though the answer means indoor plants in flowerpots.
explanation.definitionFit: Houseplants grown in containers are what this phrase normally describes.

clue.text: Fuss about poor rep's craft threatened by this

indicators.note: the fuss goes about, enclosing, the other piece

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A commotion over an incompetent salesman's boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges REP to RPE, and 'about' puts TODO round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater missile is the weapon a ship fears from submarines.

clue.text: Green growth could make it a wearisome task to get into shelter

indicators.note: the task gets into the shelter, sitting inside it

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side
FAG is British slang for a tedious chore

explanation.surface: A tired worker finds refuge among the leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: FAG in British English means a tiresome job; A + FAG goes inside LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliage is collectively the leaves of plants, their green growth.

clue.text: Murderer retains right to have mark of respect

indicators.note: the murderer retains, holding inside, the letter for right

parts.note: Cain murdered his brother Abel in Genesis

explanation.surface: A killer keeps the right to be honoured.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile of stones is raised as a memorial or landmark.

clue.text: Boast to lawyers which gives lots of leverage

parts.note: to crow is to boast
the bar is the legal profession

explanation.surface: Bragging to the legal profession for influence.
explanation.definitionFit: This iron lever is used to prise things open.

clue.text: Documents primitive instincts with clubs?

parts.note: in Freudian psychology the id is the primitive instinctive mind
clubs is a suit of playing cards

explanation.surface: Papers relating to cavemen and their clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Identity cards are official papers proving who someone is.

clue.text: Advances leaving no way out?

parts.note: split as in plus roads, these would be roads going only inwards; the real sense is progress made into territory

explanation.surface: A question about an army's progress that blocks retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as IN ROADS: routes in only, with no way out.
explanation.definitionFit: Making progress into a market or territory is gaining ground.

clue.text: Guarantor has no right to get fat

indicators.note: 'has no right' tells us to remove the letter for right from the guarantor

parts.note: a surety is a person who guarantees another

explanation.surface: A guarantor without rights grows plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Resembling or containing hard animal fat makes something greasy or fatty.

clue.text: Print made smaller to fit on box

indicators.note: the second piece is set on after the first

parts.note: box is a type of wood
cut means made smaller

explanation.surface: A print reduced in size to go on a box.
explanation.walkthrough: Box is a hardwood tree, so box gives WOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraving made on a wooden block produces a print.

clue.text: Raise European tax in general

indicators.note: 'in' places the tax inside the general

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A call to increase EU taxes across the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in general' looks like a phrase meaning overall; general is LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something up is to elevate it.

clue.text: Put ban on Spain's doctor joining old Greek boat

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A Spanish doctor boards an ancient ship, prompting a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: An official prohibition on trade is imposed on something banned.

clue.text: They want partners to have singletons in red suits?

parts.note: singletons, people on their own, are lonely
hearts is one of the red suits in cards

explanation.surface: Single people at the card table wishing for a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonely hearts are those seeking romance through personal ads.
